title: Building a Complete Beginner Prompt Framework
introduction: This lesson shows how to combine basic prompting ideas into a simple, reusable framework. By following the steps you can write clear, structured prompts for education, business, personal tasks, and creative work.

sections.heading: Start with a Clear Goal
sections.subheading: What you want the AI to achieve
paragraphs: Begin every prompt by stating the exact purpose. A clear goal tells the AI the main task it should focus on.
A well‑defined goal reduces ambiguity and leads to more useful answers.

example.title: Goal Example: Summarize a news article
example.content: Prompt: "Summarize the main points of the article about climate change in three sentences."

sections.heading: Provide Context and Choose a Role
sections.subheading: Give background and tell the AI how to act
paragraphs: Context supplies the necessary background information so the AI understands the situation.
Assigning a role (like teacher, marketer, or friend) guides the tone and style of the response.

example.title: Context and Role Example: Teacher explaining a concept
example.content: Prompt: "You are a friendly middle school teacher. Explain photosynthesis in simple terms for 12‑year‑olds."

sections.heading: List Inputs, Constraints, and Process Steps
sections.subheading: Specify data, limits, and how the AI should work
paragraphs: Inputs are the pieces of information the AI needs to use, such as dates, numbers, or text snippets.
Constraints set limits (time, length, format) and process steps tell the AI how to think through the task.

example.title: Inputs and Constraints Example: Creating a study schedule
example.content: Prompt: "Create a weekly study schedule for a college student who has classes on Monday, Wednesday, Friday from 9 am‑12 pm, and wants to study 10 hours total. Limit each study block to 2 hours and include short breaks."

sections.heading: Define the Desired Output Format
sections.subheading: Tell the AI exactly how the answer should look
paragraphs: Specify whether you need a list, a table, bullet points, or a paragraph. This makes the result ready to use.
Clear formatting instructions avoid extra editing after the AI responds.

example.title: Output Format Example: Bullet list of marketing ideas
example.content: Prompt: "List five creative social media campaign ideas for a new coffee shop. Present each idea as a bullet point with a short description."

sections.heading: Create a Reusable Prompt Template
sections.subheading: Combine all parts into one flexible structure
paragraphs: Use the same headings—Goal, Context, Role, Inputs, Constraints, Process, Output format—to build a template you can fill in for any task.
Having a template saves time and ensures consistency across different prompts.

example.title: Template Example: Personal productivity prompt
example.content:
Template:
Goal: ...
Context: ...
Role: ...
Inputs: ...
Constraints: ...
Process: ...
Output format: ...
Fill in each section for the specific task you need.

practice.title: Build Your Own Prompt Template
practice.instruction: Choose a simple daily task (for example, planning a grocery list). Write a prompt using the framework: state the goal, give context, assign a role if helpful, list inputs, add any constraints, describe the process, and specify the output format. Keep it short and imagine the AI’s response.

keyTakeaways: A good prompt starts with a clear goal that tells the AI what to do.
Adding context and a role helps the AI produce answers that match the intended style.
Specifying inputs, constraints, and process steps guides the AI’s reasoning and limits.
Defining the output format ensures the answer is ready to use.
A reusable template lets you quickly create structured prompts for many tasks.

mcqs.question: What is the first step when creating a prompt according to the lesson?
mcqs.explanation: The lesson says every prompt should begin by stating the exact purpose, which is the clear goal.

mcqs.question: Why is assigning a role to the AI useful?
options: It changes the AI's underlying model
mcqs.explanation: A role tells the AI how to act, influencing the tone and style of the response.

mcqs.question: Which part of the framework is used to limit the number of items in a list or the length of the answer?
mcqs.explanation: Constraints set limits such as time, length, or number of items.

mcqs.question: In the reusable prompt template, which heading follows "Inputs"?
mcqs.explanation: The template order is Goal, Context, Role, Inputs, Constraints, Process, Output format; so Constraints comes after Inputs.

mcqs.question: What is the main purpose of defining the desired output format?
options: To make the AI think faster
To ensure the answer is ready to use
mcqs.explanation: Specifying the format (list, table, bullet points, etc.) makes the result usable without extra editing.
